content.comment_body: Good afternoon, is it possible to show the text message currently displayed on the [product_name] device screen on the [product_name] web page?
Could this feature be suggested to [company_name] so that error and fault messages could be displayed, as it would be beneficial for future use?
Why? You can create custom message texts in [product_name] web editor.

You can make custom texts, but they won't show up automatically when a memory is activated. For example, if a fault occurs and the [product_name] device displays 'low pressure', you need to add a button, update the text, insert error backgrounds, and set the text to appear when active. For multiple messages, each one requires a separate button. Overlaying them doesn't work; showing messages directly from the device display would be much simpler and more effective.

You can place static text on the interface and overlay it with a digital value. When it's 'Off', it matches the background; when 'On', a transparent image appears, revealing the text. Would you like an example?
How would you handle multiple messages? You have to keep stacking them below each other, and space constraints can be an issue.
I'm facing the same problem. An example would be helpful—I might be able to adapt it to my project.
Can you explain in more detail what exactly you're trying to achieve?

You need to recreate the error messages and cover them with a background-colored box, which turns transparent when the input is active. Stack each message underneath the previous one, as overlapping them doesn't work. Hopefully, this will be improved in the future.
You can log in normally without enabling website customization. The current [product_name] display can be viewed just like the actual [product_name] device. You can also confirm messages as needed.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are looking for a way to display system error or fault messages from the physical [product_name] device directly on the [product_name] web interface. Since there's no direct synchronization, messages must be manually recreated with workarounds to indicate errors. This process is made more difficult due to layout restrictions and limited space, especially when multiple error messages are involved.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope that error and fault messages shown natively on their [product_name] device screens can be conveniently and automatically reflected on the [product_name] web page, eliminating the need for manual re-entry and offering better efficiency, particularly when managing several messages.
